title: Localization and suspension criterion for a pointed model category
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete category, in particular admitting finite limits and colimits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], with a zero object and a model structure: classes of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences, the latter closed under retracts and satisfying two-out-of-three, with weak factorization systems (cofibration, trivial fibration) and (trivial cofibration, fibration), and functorial factorizations. Trivial means also a weak equivalence; a weak factorization system means factorization of every map and mutually characterized diagonal lifting classes. An object is cofibrant if the map from zero is a cofibration. Let $\mathcal M_\infty$ be the homotopy coherent localization at the weak equivalences, meaning the universal homotopy theory in which these maps are inverted, retaining mapping spaces and composition homotopies. Then $\mathcal M_\infty$ has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and its ordinary homotopy category is the ordinary localization of $\mathcal M$ at its weak equivalences. A span of cofibrant objects whose two outgoing maps are cofibrations has its homotopy pushout represented by its ordinary pushout. Its suspension functor $\Sigma$ is the homotopy pushout $0\coprod_X^h0$ and is left adjoint to the loop functor given by the homotopy pullback $0\times_X^h0$. If the induced suspension on the ordinary homotopy category is an equivalence, $\mathcal M_\infty$ is stable: a square is a homotopy pushout exactly when it is a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Agent-formulated generic homotopy-theoretic foundation for the stable enhancement of proof paragraph 2. No Stacks tag supplies the coherent stability criterion. Independently checked: Lurie, Higher Algebra (August 3, 2012), Proposition 1.4.2.11 and Corollary 1.4.2.27, https://people.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/papers/HA2012.pdf, give the infinity-categorical suspension criterion; the model-localization comparison remains part of the stated foundation.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal M_\infty$ and let $q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal C$ be localization. The homotopy category has the same objects and morphism sets $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)$. For any ordinary category $D$, a functor from $\mathcal C$ to its nerve is exactly a functor $h\mathcal C\to D$: all higher homotopies become the equalities of composition. The localization universal property therefore identifies functors $h\mathcal C\to D$ with functors $\mathcal M\to D$ that invert weak equivalences, including their natural transformations. This is precisely the ordinary localization universal property, proving $h\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$.

source.place: Agent argument from the two localization universal properties; this is the homotopy-category comparison in the item.

proof.text: Consider the direct category $I=(b\leftarrow a\to c)$, with degrees $0$ at $a$ and $1$ at $b,c$. By [lem-coef-finite-reedy-localization], every coherent span in $\mathcal C$ is represented up to coherent equivalence by a strict span $B\leftarrow A\to C$ in $\mathcal M$. Factor $0\to A$ as a cofibration $0\to QA$ followed by a trivial fibration $QA\to A$, and factor the composites $QA\to B,C$ as cofibrations $QA\to B',C'$ followed by trivial fibrations $B'\to B,C'\to C$. This is an objectwise weak equivalence of spans. Its latching maps are $0\to QA$, $QA\to B'$, $QA\to C'$, so it is Reedy cofibrant. The derived colimit adjunction of the cited lemma says that $B'\coprod_{QA}C'$ with its cocone represents the pushout of the original coherent span, since being left adjoint to the constant diagram is the mapping-space universal property of colimit. For a given span of cofibrant objects with both outgoing maps cofibrations, those three latching maps are already cofibrations; its ordinary pushout itself thus represents its homotopy pushout. No left properness is used.

source.place: Agent construction using finite direct Reedy localization, supplying homotopy pushouts for the stable flat-model foundation of paragraph 2.

proof.text: Dually take $J=(a\to c\leftarrow b)$, with degree $1$ at $a,b$ and $0$ at $c$. Its inverse-diagram comparison in [lem-coef-finite-reedy-localization] represents any coherent cospan by $A\to C\leftarrow B$. Choose a fibrant replacement $C\to RC$ by factoring $C\to0$ into a trivial cofibration and a fibration, and factor $A\to RC$ and $B\to RC$ into trivial cofibrations $A\to A'$, $B\to B'$ and fibrations $A'\to RC$, $B'\to RC$. The matching maps are $RC\to0$, $A'\to RC$, $B'\to RC$; hence the replacement cospan is Reedy fibrant. The cited infinity adjunction identifies $A'\times_{RC}B'$ and its cone with the pullback. This proves existence of all homotopy pullbacks without right properness.

source.place: Agent dual inverse-Reedy construction for the finite homotopy limits used in paragraph 2.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-finite-reedy-localization] also with the empty category, which is both direct and inverse. There is a unique empty diagram and its replacements are itself. Its ordinary colimit is the initial object $0$ of $\mathcal M$, and its ordinary limit is the terminal object, the same $0$. The two derived adjunctions show that $q(0)$ is initial and terminal in $\mathcal C$, so it is a zero object in the mapping-space sense. Combining this with the pushouts of Step 2 and pullbacks of Step 3, [lem-coef-infinity-finite-shape-generation] gives all finite homotopy colimits and limits. This uses finite coherent shapes, rather than claiming that finite limits in $h\mathcal C$ are homotopy limits.

source.place: Agent passage from empty/span/cospan shapes to finite coherent (co)limits; HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4 and its dual, checked online, not archived.

proof.text:
Define $\Sigma X=0\coprod_X^h0$ and $\Omega Y=0\times_Y^h0$, functorially by their universal properties. The natural mapping-space identities are
$$\operatorname{Map}(\Sigma X,Y)\simeq *\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)}*\simeq\operatorname{Map}(X,\Omega Y).$$
The first is the pushout universal property with the two contractible spaces $\operatorname{Map}(0,Y)$; the second is the pullback universal property with the two contractible spaces $\operatorname{Map}(X,0)$. Basepoints are the zero morphisms. These natural equivalences are the definition of an infinity-categorical adjunction $\Sigma\dashv\Omega$. In particular its unit $\eta_X:X\to\Omega\Sigma X$ is the map supplied by the suspension square, with its canonical nullhomotopies; its counit is the dual map. On $\pi_0$ this gives an ordinary adjunction on $h\mathcal C$.

source.place: Agent verification of the suspension-loop adjunction from mapping-space universal properties, following the pointed constructions of HA 1.4.2.

proof.text: Assume now $h\Sigma$ is an equivalence. Its full faithfulness makes the ordinary adjunction unit an isomorphism, as follows explicitly. For an ordinary adjunction $L\dashv R$ with fully faithful $L$, choose $r:RLX\to X$ with $Lr=\epsilon_{LX}$ by fullness. The first triangle identity and faithfulness give $r\eta_X=1$. Naturality and the second triangle give $\eta_Xr=RLr\,\eta_{RLX}=R\epsilon_{LX}\,\eta_{RLX}=1$. The counit is then invertible at every $LX$ by the first triangle, and at every object by essential surjectivity of $L$ and naturality. Apply this to $h\Sigma\dashv h\Omega$. A morphism in an infinity category is an equivalence exactly when its class in its homotopy category is invertible. Thus every actual unit and counit component of Step 5 is an equivalence. They are coherent natural transformations from that adjunction, and give inverse equivalences $\Sigma,\Omega$ on $\mathcal C$, not just on its homotopy category.

source.place: Agent explicit unit/counit argument that upgrades the assumed equivalence on the homotopy category to the suspension-loop equivalence.

proof.text: Let $\tau=(W\to X,W\to Y,X\to Z,Y\to Z)$ be an arbitrary homotopy pushout square of $\mathcal C$, and put $P=X\times_Z^hY$, $a:W\to P$. Apply [lem-coef-suspension-square-comparison] with both categories equal to $\mathcal C$ and $F=\mathrm{id}$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 4; $F$ is reduced since it fixes zero. It supplies $\theta:P\to\Omega\Sigma W$, with $\theta a\simeq\eta_W$ and $(\Omega a_{\Sigma\tau})\theta\simeq u$. Here $u:P\to\Omega\Sigma X\times_{\Omega\Sigma Z}^h\Omega\Sigma Y$ is the map on pullbacks of the unit maps at $X,Y,Z$. Those three unit maps are equivalences by Step 6, so $u$ is an equivalence: their inverses are a coherent inverse transformation, and taking the pullback gives inverse maps on these two pullbacks. The loop on $a_{\Sigma\tau}$ is essential for the second composite to have the displayed domain.

source.place: Agent application of the technical comparison of HA Lemma 1.4.2.15, with its suspended comparison written with the required loop.

proof.text: The equations of Step 7 give a right inverse $r=a\eta_W^{-1}$ for $\theta$, and a left inverse $l=u^{-1}\Omega a_{\Sigma\tau}$ for $\theta$. In the homotopy category, $l=l(\theta r)=(l\theta)r=r$, so $\theta$ is invertible, hence an equivalence. Since $\theta a=\eta_W$ and $\eta_W$ is an equivalence, $a$ is an equivalence as well. That is exactly the pullback universal property for $\tau$. This proves that every homotopy pushout square is a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Agent inverse calculation, the retract argument in the proof of HA Proposition 1.4.2.13; no excision criterion is used as a black box.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal E=\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. By Step 4 it is pointed and has finite limits and colimits, with their roles exchanged. Its suspension is $(\Omega_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, its loop is $(\Sigma_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and its adjunction unit $\eta^{\mathcal E}$ is the opposite of the counit of Step 5, hence has equivalence components by Step 6. For any pushout square $\tau$ in $\mathcal E$, put $P=X\times_ZY$ and let $a:W\to P$ be its comparison. Apply [lem-coef-suspension-square-comparison] to the identity of $\mathcal E$, obtaining $\theta:P\to\Omega_{\mathcal E}\Sigma_{\mathcal E}W$ with $\theta a\simeq\eta^{\mathcal E}_W$ and $b\theta\simeq u$, where $b=\Omega_{\mathcal E}a_{\Sigma_{\mathcal E}\tau}$ and $u$ is the map between pullbacks induced by $\eta^{\mathcal E}$ at $X,Y,Z$. The inverse natural transformation to $\eta^{\mathcal E}$ induces the inverse map between these pullbacks, so $u$ is an equivalence. Set $r=a(\eta^{\mathcal E}_W)^{-1}$ and $l=u^{-1}b$. In $h\mathcal E$ we have $\theta r=1$, $l\theta=1$ and $l=l(\theta r)=(l\theta)r=r$. Therefore $\theta$ is invertible, and $a=\theta^{-1}\eta^{\mathcal E}_W$ is invertible. Thus the square is a pullback in $\mathcal E$. A pullback in $\mathcal C$ is a pushout in $\mathcal E$, so this proves that every homotopy pullback in $\mathcal C$ is a homotopy pushout. Step 8 gives the other implication.

source.place: Agent dual comparison argument for the reverse implication; HA Proposition 1.4.2.11 explains the opposite-category passage.
